features.text: Patient has been struggling with asthma for the past six months.
Patient experiences asthma flare-ups almost every month or every other month.
Patient uses a blue inhaler called Ventolin almost every day and a couple of times a week at night.
Patient has undergone a pulmonary function test, which was consistent with asthma.
Patient has not had any imaging studies done for asthma.
Patient's asthma flares up when getting sick with a cold and possibly due to exposure to her aunt's cat.
Patient avoids going to her aunt's house to reduce exposure to the cat.
Patient's symptoms occur almost every month or every other month, with daily inhaler use and night-time use a couple of times a week.
Patient does not use any controller medications, only the blue inhaler Ventolin.
Patient has not had any allergy testing, such as skin prick tests or IgE blood tests, for common allergens like cat dander, dust mites, pollen, or mold.
Patient has not undergone any pulmonary function tests or spirometry reviewed by a pulmonologist.
Patient has not been evaluated by a pulmonologist or allergist for asthma management.
Patient has not had any pulmonary function tests or peak flow monitoring to assess asthma control and severity.
Patient experiences coughing, wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath during flare-ups, especially at night.
Patient's asthma symptoms wake her up a couple of times a week.
Patient uses an inhaler to get back to sleep during flare-ups.
Patient is an adult female with a regular office job.
Patient does not have any specific issues with her job that seem to trigger her asthma.
Patient wants to start hiking again without worrying about asthma flaring up.
